ground_truth_evidence: category 5: the dataset's own trigger (newplatform_bundles/conversion/c5/gt/jq/vulnerability_FZ_13/args.txt; adapted: exploit.sh runs `jq -n '.foo'` on `{}`; the ground truth is the two argv lines `-n` and `{}|.foo` (the object is built inline with -n so no stdin is needed). HOME is unset by the judge so jq's implicit ~/.jq import is skipped; otherwise that import crashes the vulnerable build on any program (degenerate). exploit.sh's own input.json is generated by the script, so nothing was lost but a recorded run.)

category5.design: The injected code makes jvp_object_read return &slot->value even when the key is missing (slot==NULL), so jv_object_get on a missing key reads near NULL. The PoC is the jq argv; `-n '{}|.foo'` looks up a missing key on an object and crashes the vulnerable build, while the secure build returns null. HOME is unset so the crash comes only from the filter, not from jq's implicit ~/.jq import (which would make any program crash).
